To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose a novel attributed stochastic block model that can be used to learn the community structure of a network from both connectivity and attribute data; 2) we show that the attributed stochastic block can be used to perform link prediction and collaborative prediction tasks in the event of missing connectivity or attribute data, respectively; 3) the attributed stochastic block provides better performance than the standard stochastic block model in both tasks; and 4) the attributed stochastic model provides satisfactory performance on biological networks.

we propose an augmented stochastic block model for networks with multiple continuous attributes and we demonstrate the utility of this model in the link prediction task and collaborative filtering task.
the attributed stochastic block models provide a framework for learning the community structure of a network when the nodes are associated with continuous attributes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: can we improve the performance of community detection algorithms by augmenting the adjacency matrix with continuous attribute vectors associated with the nodes?
a stochastic block model with multiple continuous attributes that is used to learn community structure and the associated parameters in the multivariate Gaussian models describing each community.
the following question: can we improve community detection by augmenting connectivity with additional continuous attribute information?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed attributed stochastic block model is useful for predicting network structure when one has access to the attribute information for the nodes in the network.
the attributed stochastic block models provide an effective way to integrate multiple sources of data in order to perform community detection and prediction tasks.
this work provides a new method for community detection and network prediction in the context of attributed networks, which is useful for many applications in the biological sciences.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel model to incorporate continuous attribute information in the stochastic block model, and demonstrated its usefulness in two network prediction tasks.

our model is the most general stochastic block model to date and that the model can provide satisfactory performance for link prediction and collaborative prediction tasks in the presence of multiple continuous attributes.

the augmented stochastic block model is a flexible model for learning community structure in networks that can also predict the attributes or connectivity patterns of a new node in an unsupervised fashion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the attributed stochastic block models provide a flexible framework to learn community structure and node attributes in the same probabilistic framework.
the stochastic block model can be extended in a principled way to handle multiple continuous node attributes.
the attributed stochastic block models can be used to improve the performance of community detection methods when there is additional information in the form of node attributes.
